text: `ResolvedProgram::build` resolves dependency bodies whenever `profile.dependency_bodies == Keep`, tying a retention choice (keep trees) to a meaning choice (resolve and attach dependency call-site edges). A FULL caller that only needs trees pays `resolve_dependency_bodies`; a single-app FULL caller would silently get dependency edges.
evidence: | CR1 | important | fixed | b8b59b5a | Real. `ResolvedProgram::build(inputs, ProgramScope)` (resolved.rs:38, :204): `Workspace` = Summary profile and no dependency edges; `CrossApp` = FULL + `resolve_dependency_bodies`. The profile is derived from the scope (`ProgramScope::profile`), so no caller can ask for one without the other. The meta records the scope. | Type change: there is no way left to pass a profile, so no runtime test. Callers: run.rs (both arms), impact_graph (`CrossApp`), aldump --compiler-oracle (CR13). |

text: The pub `export_from_program` takes any `ResolvedProgram`, but `ProgramMeta` does not record its profile. Given a Summary-built program the graph silently drops every dependency call-site edge and `dependencyBodies` reads zeros; it also panics via `expect("export reads the body")` although it returns Result.
evidence: | CR2 | important | fixed | b8b59b5a | Real. `export_from_program` (impact_graph/mod.rs:203) returns `Err("the call-graph export needs a cross-app program build …")` unless `meta.scope == CrossApp`; the body is no longer an Option, so the `expect` is gone (CR8). | Test `cli_graph_export::export_refuses_a_workspace_scoped_program` (same workspace: Workspace refused, CrossApp ok). Break (Edit, guard made `&& false`): FAILED, panic `reading dependency trees needs DependencyBodies::Keep` (full.rs:1572), i.e. the old silent/panicking path. Reverted: ok. Log H:/al-sem-160-bench/p3-break.log. |

text: The `inputs` bucket is `Kind::Exact`, but it counts a serde_json Map (BTreeMap) as one flat buffer and never walks `al_walk`'s `Arc<io::Error>`, so it is not exact as census.rs defines the word.
evidence: | CR4 | minor | fixed (docs) | b8b59b5a | Real as a wording gap. census.rs:17 now states the `inputs` bucket's two under-counts (the `app.json` maps' B-tree nodes, an `io::Error` payload), next to the existing exception, and sizes them (a few hundred bytes against the workspace texts). The bucket stays `exact` because it is exact for what makes it (the texts). | Docs only. |

text: `ProgramBody::edge_view(primary_app_ref)` takes the primary app as a parameter although the context and the meta hold it; a wrong AppRef silently misclassifies primary and dependency nodes.
evidence: | CR5 | minor | fixed | b8b59b5a | Real. `edge_view(&self)` (resolved.rs:135) reads `self.ctx.primary_app_ref`; `ProgramMeta.primary_app_ref` is removed, so there is one source. | Signature change: a caller can no longer pass a different app. No runtime test. |

text: `attach_program_calls(_with)` take `inputs` and `coverage` separately though every caller passes the meta's; run.rs deep-clones `FreshCoverage` where it used to move it.

text: `body: Option<ProgramBody>` forces `.take().expect`/`.as_ref().expect` at 4 sites, turning a type rule into runtime panics; a second consumer of a shared program (#160's batch goal) panics.
evidence: | CR8 | important | fixed | b8b59b5a | Real. `body: ProgramBody` (resolved.rs:63). Readers borrow `&ResolvedProgram`; `attach_program_calls` consumes it and hands back the meta, and `ProgramBody::release` drops it in the old span order (`b3.report_drop`, `b3.ctx_drop`). A read after the release does not compile. | Compile-time rule; no runtime test can express it. |

text: `loaded_apps(&ctx, &coverage)` is computed for every build, including single-app Summary builds where nothing reads it.
evidence: | CR9 | minor | fixed | b8b59b5a | Real. `ResolvedProgram::loaded_apps()` (resolved.rs:269) computes it on demand while the body is alive; its two readers (the graph export and the cross-app arm) call it. | Behaviour-preserving. Graph golden and suite green. |

text: The head digest is 7.9 s slower (median), slower in 5 of 6 interleaved pairs, `crossapp.context_build` +3.3 s; the doc calls it cone noise without finding a cause.
evidence: | CR10 | minor | refuted (the slowdown); fixed (the doc) | this run | The finding was right that 5 of 6 is not proof of noise, so 14 more interleaved digest pairs were run on CDO against the same parent 576dd296. r1 (8 pairs, the same 1d4b6bf7 binary the doc measured): parent median 68.7 s, head 63.1 s, head slower in 1 of 8. r2 (6 pairs, final head b8b59b5a, analyze and digest alternating, side order flipped per round): digest 64.8 vs 64.8 s (+0.1, 3 of 6), analyze 37.7 vs 38.5 s (+0.8, 2 of 6). crossapp.context_build medians -0.6 s (r1, 3 of 8) and -0.3 s (r2, 4 of 6). So there is no head slowdown; the original 5-of-6 did not repeat. The step 1b doc now records both benches and re-checks A1b.4 on b8b59b5a (all four peaks met, -4.5 to +2.5 MB), SARIF and digest bytes and the CDO histogram SHA unchanged. | H:/al-sem-160-bench/r1, r2 (runs.jsonl + traces); scripts/bench_ab.py summary and trace_summary.py --compare. |
